Order dated 22 December 1787- conveying Thomas Parkinson, a vagrant, from Bowes to Blewgrass in Westmorland.  Order dated 20 October 1787- conveying Elizabeth Glover, a vagrant, from the township of Bowes to Whitby.  Order dated 22 December 1787- conveying Milkey Clayton and Susana her infant child, both vagrants, from the township of Bowes to Boroughbridge in the West Riding.  Order dated 22 December 1787- conveying Anne Clayton and her son, both vagrants, from the township of Bowes to Boroughbridge in the West Riding.  Order dated 22 December 1787- conveying Anne Dawes, a vagrant, from the township of Bowes to Boroughbridge in the West Riding.  Order dated 22 December 1787- conveying Thomas Bubb, Mary his wife, and Mary, Elizabeth and Anne their daughters, from the township of Bowes to the town of Boroughbridge in the West Riding.  Order dated 11 January 1788

title: Order for a payment for bridge repairs
description: Note from John Carr at York to the Clerk of the Peace at Malton.  There are many bridges to be repaired, and Whitby Bridge repairs have cost £196.  Henry King must have an order on the treasurer for £200 at the present Sessions at Malton

title: Bastardy recognizance for the child of Mary Outhwaite of Fylingdales
description: Recognizance made by Joseph Earl blacksmith, John Denton alum maker, and William Brunton yeoman. all of the township of Fylingdales, for the appearance of Earl at the next Quarter Sessions as father of the bastard child of Mary Outhwaite of the township of Fylingdales singlewoman, which when born is likely to be chargeable to the township of Whitby [sic]

title: Bastardy recognizance for the child of Ann Hardy of Whitby
description: Recognizance made by William Stangoe mariner, Thomas Blyth weaver, and George Craig weaver, all of Whitby, for the appearance of Stangoe at the next Quarter Sessions as father of the bastard child of Ann Hardy of the township of Whitby widow, which when born is likely to be chargeable to the township of Whitby

title: Copy indictment for not repairing the king's highway: the inhabitants of Hartoft
description: Copy indictment of the inhabitants of the township of Hartoft for not repairing part of the highway from the market town of Kirby Moorside to the market town of Whitby. From 20 November 1787 the highway has been in disrepair from the limits of the township of Rosedale East Side extending northwards towards the limits of the parish of Egton at the extremity of the township of Hartoft, being 1,500 yards in length and seven yards in breadth. Endorsed "New Malton Christmas Sessions 15th January 1788"

title: Copy indictment for not repairing the king's highway: the inhabitants of Egton
description: Copy indictment of the inhabitants of the township of Egton for not repairing part of the highway from the market town of Kirby Moorside to the market town of Whitby. From 20 November 1787 the highway has been in disrepair from the limits of the township of Hartoft extending towards a bridge called Egton Bridge in the parish of Egton, being 5,000 yards in length and seven yards in breadth. Endorsed "New Malton Christmas Sessions 15th January 1788"

title: Copy indictment for not repairing the king's highway: the inhabitants of Rosedale East Side
description: Copy indictment of the inhabitants of the township of Rosedale East Side for not repairing part of the highway leading from the market town of Kirby Moorside to the market town of Whitby. From 20 November 1788 the highway has been in disrepair in the township of Rosedale East Side from a place called Rosedale Abbey, extending towards the limits of the township of Hartoft at the extremity of the township of Rosedale East Side, being 3,000 yards in length and seven yards in breadth. Endorsed "New Malton Christmas Sessions 15th January 1788"

title: Recognizances in the case against Isaac Wilson of Robin Hood's Town

title: Bill of indictment for felony: Ann Wriglesworth of Whitby

title: Bill of indictment for felony: John Garbut of Whitby
description: Bill of indictment of John Garbut late of the township of Whitby labourer for stealing one linen shirt value 10d, the property of Francis Johnson. Offence committed at the township of Whitby on 8 January 1788. Endorsed with names of witnesses and "a true bill"

title: Bill of indictment for felony: George Child of Whitby
description: Bill of indictment of George Child late of the township of Whitby mariner for stealing one pair of silver knee buckles value 3d, one pair of shoes value 1d, one cloth coat value 1d, one everlasting jacket value 1d, one pair of breeches value 1d, one pair of trousers value 1d, three linen shirts value 1d, and one silk handkerchief value 1d, the property of George Reed. description: Bill of indictment of George Child late of the township of Whitby mariner for stealing two linen shirts value 4d and one cloth jacket value 4d, the property of Elizabeth Boulton. title: Calendar of prisoners at the House of Correction at Thirsk
description: A calendar of prisoners committed to the House of Correction at Thirsk.  Includes:- Andrew Smith, a rogue and vagabond found wandering and begging in the township of Thirsk without having a legal settlement there.  Committed on 16 October 1787- Richard Baker, charged on the oath of William Warley with stealing oak timber, the property of Mr John Bailey and Company, from a wood in Riccaldale on the night of Thursday 27 September 1787.  Committed on 18 October 1787- Peter Alloyisius Dignum, a rogue and vagabond, for threatening James Moon and his wife in the town of Loftus- Elizabeth Morril [spelled Morrell in one copy], an incorrigible rogue and vagabond, committed on 19 October 1787 by William Comber clerk to be punished according to the law- William Wood, charged by the overseers of East Ayton with deserting his wife and family, whereby they became chargeable to the parish of Ayton, and refusing to relieve them or find securities.  Committed on 5 November 1787.  Annotated "Commit's"- Christopher Clapham, charged on the oath of Mary Fawcett of the township of Thirsk with having got her with child.  Committed on 1 December 1787 for want of securities for his appearance- Ann Wriglesworth, charged with stealing a forequarter of mutton, the property of John Jackson of the township of Ugthorpe butcher, and taken from his stall in Whitby.  Committed on 22 December 1787.  Annotated "Bill found"- George Child, charged with stealing a blue grey second mourning coat and a pair of breeches, a black everlasting stuff waistcoat, a pair of blue cloth trousers, a pair of shoes, a black silk handkerchief, three blue and white striped linen shirts, and a pair of silver knee buckles, the property of George Reed of Whitby mariner; and two blue and white striped linen shirts and a cloth waistcoat, the property of Thomas Bolton of Whitby, all taken from the dwelling house of John Bolton of Whitby on the night of 22 December 1787.  Committed on 24 December 1787.  Annotated "Transports"- Michael Berwick, charged on suspicion of stealing an unbaked bread loaf and the tin it was in value 1s, the property of Henry Richardson late of Huttons Ambo.  Committed 26 December 1787- Christopher Bell, charged on the oath of Ann Nesom of the township of Northallerton with having got her with child.  Committed on 12 January 1788 for want of securities for his appearance. Prisoners for Richmond Sessions- Nathaniel Cole, a rogue and vagabond found wandering and begging in the township of Bedale, with no legal settlement there.  He pretended that he was afflicted with dropsy and had been tapped twice, but when he was examined he was reported to be an impostor, with no marks of having been tapped.  Committed on 1 November 1787- William Herren, charged on the oath of Jane Clarkson of the township of Grinton with having got her with child.  Committed on 15 November 1787 for want of sufficient sureties for his appearance- William Wood, committed on 28 November 1787 for refusing to find sureties for his appearance at the next Quarter Sessions and to keep the peace especially towards David Mankin of Smeaton- Thomas Metcalfe, charged on the oath of Ann Rawling of the township of Brompton with having got her with child.  Committed on 22 December 1787 for want of sufficient sureties for his appearance- William Hopwood, William Brown, George Bevins and James Boddy, all to remain in the House of Correction upon their orders and commitments- John Garbut, charged on violent suspicion of stealing a white linen shirt marked with the letters F.J., the property of a person unknown, on 8 January 1788.  Committed on 12 January 1788. Two copies.  One appears to have the names deleted up to the prisoners for Richmond Sessions.  The other has these same names struck through, as well as the entries for Hopwood, Brown, Bevins and Boddy.  Both copies are endorsed as a calendar from the Malton and Richmond Christmas Sessions 1788

description: Bill of indictment of Christopher Tiplady late of the House of Correction at Northallerton labourer for stealing five glass bottles value 1s, two quarts of hollands value 1s, two quarts of gin value 1s, one tin canister value 1s, and one other canister value 1s, the property of John Barry and William Gales; also one silk pocket handkerchief value 1s, one other handkerchief value 1s, three shirts value 1s, the property of Thomas Welch, taken from the schooner "John and Catherine" belonging to the port of Whitby and on the navigable River Esk. description: Bill of indictment of William Dunbar labourer and Christopher Tiplady labourer, both late of the House of Correction at Northallerton, for stealing five glass bottles value 1s, two quarts of hollands value 1s, two quarts of gin value 1s, three quarts of ale value 1s, one pound weight of tea value 1s, one pound weight of biscuits value 1s, one pound weight of treacle value 1s, one pound weight of butter value 1s, one tin canister value 1s, and ten pounds weight of pork value 1s, the property of John Barry and William Gales; also one cotton handkerchief value 1s, one other handkerchief value 1s, the property of Henry Ord; also one silk pocket handkerchief value 1s, one other handkerchief value 1s, and three shirts value 1s, the property of Thomas Welch, taken from the schooner "John and Catherine" belonging to the port of Whitby and on the navigable River Esk. title: Bill of indictment for felony: William Dunbar and Christopher Tiplady both of the House of Correction at Northallerton

title: Petition concerning Jane Coupland and Ann Coupland both of Whitby
description: Petition presented to those Justices in court at the Quarter Sessions to be held at Northallerton on 27 June 1836.  Those who have signed the petition know Jane Coupland and Ann Coupland of Whitby spinsters, who were prosecuted by Messrs Horne and Richardson of Whitby stationers at the last Christmas Quarter Sessions for receiving books, knowing them to have been stolen.  They were found guilty, and sentenced to 18 months imprisonment in the House of Correction at Northallerton.  They have served six months of their sentence and are said to have suffered greatly.  They are in a precarious state of health, which has led to deep contrition and a determination to be of good moral conduct in future.  It was their first offence, and the petitioners ask the court for a mitigation of their sentence.  Signed by 102 inhabitants of Whitby
